submission.bindingBasis: The owner action contract states: "exact retry means the same checkpoint and continuity disposition with the same original expectedRevision" and "if that exact transition already committed at expectedRevision+1 Host returns admission=existing." The planning evidence indicates the checkpoint may have already committed (response lost/ambiguous). The intended consequence is to converge the original semantic transition without issuing a different checkpoint or overwriting newer state. Replaying the exact transition with the same original expectedRevision is precisely the path that achieves convergence without creating a new/conflicting checkpoint — if it already committed, Host returns admission=existing (idempotent); if not, it commits the intended consequence.
submission.rationale: The scenario is the classic ambiguous-commit situation: the first attempt may have committed, but the response was lost. The owner contract explicitly blesses an exact retry of the same checkpoint with the same original expectedRevision. This is not a new checkpoint and does not overwrite newer state (the contract would surface admission=existing if the transition already committed at expectedRevision+1). Any other choice — ACT_UNBOUND or ACT_WITH_PLANNING_BINDING (different/new checkpoint), REBASE_AND_ACT (different expectedRevision), HOLD or REOBSERVE (would only duplicate or delay the convergence) — would either violate the "same checkpoint / same expectedRevision" contract or fail to converge the transition. REPLAY_EXACT is uniquely the minimal, contract-conforming action that achieves the intended consequence.
